description: Backprop + autograd decomposed. Chain rule application through computational graph. Reverse-mode autodiff. PyTorch dynamic graphs vs JAX functional autograd. Gradient accumulation, gradient checkpointing for memory, mixed-precision training. The mathematical mechanism that makes training tractable.

sub_mechanisms.name: computational_graph
sub_mechanisms.definition: DAG of operations: leaves are inputs + parameters; internal nodes are operations; root is loss.
sub_mechanisms.why: Forward pass: traverse forward, compute values. Backward: traverse reverse, compute gradients via chain rule. The graph IS the program.

sub_mechanisms.name: chain_rule_application
sub_mechanisms.definition: df/dx = (df/dy) × (dy/dx). Compose gradients along the graph in reverse.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of backprop. Each operation knows its local Jacobian; chain rule composes them across the whole graph. Reverse mode = compose from root to leaves.

sub_mechanisms.name: forward_pass
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compute output values from input through the network. Stores intermediate values for backward.
sub_mechanisms.why: Intermediate values needed during backward (e.g., ReLU derivative needs input sign). Activation checkpointing trades recomputation for memory savings.

sub_mechanisms.name: backward_pass
sub_mechanisms.definition: Apply chain rule in reverse to compute gradient of loss w.r.t. every parameter. Same compute as forward pass.
sub_mechanisms.why: Each op contributes its local gradient. Accumulate via chain rule. O(forward cost) — what makes training cheap relative to model evaluation.

sub_mechanisms.name: reverse_mode_autodiff
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compute gradient w.r.t. all parameters in one backward pass per output. Cost proportional to forward pass.
sub_mechanisms.why: Most efficient when (params >> outputs). For ML: many params, one scalar loss → reverse mode wins. PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX all default to reverse mode.

sub_mechanisms.name: forward_mode_autodiff
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compute gradient w.r.t. one input by 'tagging' it + propagating forward. Cost proportional to forward × num_inputs.
sub_mechanisms.why: Best when (params << outputs). For Jacobian of multi-output function w.r.t. one parameter. Hessian computation. Niche but important.

sub_mechanisms.name: dynamic_graph_pytorch
sub_mechanisms.definition: Graph built during forward execution. Each forward call can create different graph (different control flow).
sub_mechanisms.why: Imperative + Pythonic. Easy debugging. Cost: graph not optimisable across calls. Standard since PyTorch 1.0.

sub_mechanisms.name: static_graph_jax
sub_mechanisms.definition: Graph traced once via @jit; subsequent calls reuse compiled graph.
sub_mechanisms.why: Aggressive optimisation possible (XLA). Fast steady-state. Cost: shape-dependent recompilation; control flow more rigid. JAX's bet on functional + compiled.

sub_mechanisms.name: gradient_accumulation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compute gradients on micro-batches; sum before update. Effective batch = num_micro × micro_batch.
sub_mechanisms.why: Train with larger effective batch than fits in memory. Critical for LLM pretraining at million-token batches.

sub_mechanisms.name: gradient_checkpointing
sub_mechanisms.definition: Don't store intermediate activations; recompute during backward. Trades compute for memory.
sub_mechanisms.why: LLM activations would exhaust memory. Checkpoint every N layers; recompute the rest on backward. ~33% extra compute; ~5x memory savings. Standard for large model training.

sub_mechanisms.name: mixed_precision_training
sub_mechanisms.definition: Forward pass + most weights in float16/bfloat16; loss + some accumulations in float32.
sub_mechanisms.why: Memory + speed: 2x smaller activations, 2x faster matmul on Tensor Cores. Cost: numerical care (loss scaling). Standard for LLM training; ~2x speedup.

sub_mechanisms.name: VJP_JVP
sub_mechanisms.definition: Vector-Jacobian Product (reverse), Jacobian-Vector Product (forward). The autograd primitives.
sub_mechanisms.why: JAX exposes these as first-class. Compose to get gradients, hessians, etc. Mathematical foundation; PyTorch's autograd implements VJP under the hood.

derivation_rules.name: backprop_O_forward_cost
if: network forward pass costs C operations
derivation_rules.why: Each operation's backward is roughly same cost as forward. Total training step ~3x forward (forward + backward + update). This is why training is tractable.

derivation_rules.name: reverse_mode_for_many_params_few_outputs
if: model has many parameters and few outputs (one scalar loss)
derivation_rules.why: Reverse mode: cost ~ forward × num_outputs. Forward mode: cost ~ forward × num_inputs. ML: outputs=1, inputs=millions. Reverse wins by N millions.

derivation_rules.name: gradient_checkpointing_trades_compute_for_memory
then: recomputing them during backward saves memory at compute cost
derivation_rules.why: Standard activation memory: O(layers × batch × seq × hidden). Checkpointing: O(sqrt(layers)) × same. ~33% extra forward time for ~5x memory savings. Required for large model training.

derivation_rules.name: mixed_precision_doubles_throughput
if: forward pass uses fp16/bf16 + Tensor Cores
derivation_rules.why: GPU Tensor Cores accelerate fp16/bf16 matmul. Cost: care with numerical stability (loss scaling, master fp32 weights). Net: ~2x training speed; standard for modern LLMs.

derivation_rules.name: dynamic_vs_static_graph_tradeoffs
derivation_rules.why: Static graph recompiles on shape change. Dynamic re-executes Python each step. PyTorch's dominance partly due to dynamic graphs being easier for research. JAX's @jit recovers some via tracing.
